title: Structural Organisation in Animals
description: Grade 11 Biology: the four animal tissues (epithelial, connective, muscular, neural) and the morphology and organ systems of the earthworm, cockroach and frog.

topics.title: Animal Tissues
topics.concept:
A group of similar cells performing a specific function is a tissue. Animal tissues are of four basic types: epithelial, connective, muscular and neural.

  • Epithelial tissue — covers body surfaces, lines organs and cavities, and forms glands. The cells are tightly packed with little material between them and rest on a basement membrane. Simple epithelium is a single layer (squamous — flat; cuboidal; columnar; ciliated), used for protection, secretion and absorption; compound epithelium has many layers, for protection (e.g. skin). Tight junctions, adhering junctions and gap junctions hold and connect the cells.
  • Connective tissue — the most abundant and widely distributed tissue; it links and supports other tissues. Its cells are loosely spaced in a matrix (jelly-like, fluid or solid). Types: loose connective (areolar, adipose/fat-storing), dense connective (tendons join muscle to bone; ligaments join bone to bone), and specialised connective — cartilage (flexible, e.g. ear, nose), bone (hard, with calcium salts, for support) and blood (a fluid connective tissue that transports materials).
  • Muscular tissue — made of long contractile cells (muscle fibres) that bring about movement. Skeletal (striated) muscle is attached to bones and is voluntary; smooth (unstriated) muscle is in the walls of internal organs and is involuntary; cardiac muscle is in the heart wall, striated but involuntary.
  • Neural tissue — made of neurons (which receive and transmit impulses) and supporting glial cells; it controls and coordinates body activities.

examples.problem: Example 1: Name the four types of animal tissue.
examples.solution:
There are four basic animal tissues.

  • Epithelial, connective, muscular and neural tissue.
examples.answer: Epithelial, connective, muscular and neural tissue.

examples.problem: Example 2: Distinguish a tendon from a ligament.
examples.solution:
Both are dense connective tissues but join different parts.

  • A tendon connects muscle to bone.
  • A ligament connects bone to bone.
examples.answer: A tendon joins muscle to bone; a ligament joins bone to bone.

examples.problem: Example 3: Compare skeletal and cardiac muscle in terms of striation and control.
examples.solution:
Both are striated but differ in control.

  • Skeletal muscle: striated and voluntary (under our will).
  • Cardiac muscle: striated but involuntary (heart works on its own).
examples.answer: Both are striated; skeletal muscle is voluntary, while cardiac muscle is involuntary.

recap:
• Four animal tissues: epithelial (covering/lining/glands), connective (link & support), muscular (movement), neural (control).
  • Connective: loose (areolar, adipose), dense (tendon muscle-to-bone, ligament bone-to-bone), specialised (cartilage, bone, blood).
  • Muscle: skeletal (striated, voluntary), smooth (unstriated, involuntary), cardiac (striated, involuntary).
  • Neural tissue = neurons + glial cells.

quiz.q: A tendon, which connects muscle to bone, is a type of:
quiz.explanation: Tendons are dense connective tissue joining muscle to bone.

quiz.q: Which muscle is striated but involuntary?
quiz.explanation: Cardiac muscle (heart) is striated yet works involuntarily.

topics.title: Morphology of the Earthworm and Cockroach
topics.concept:
Earthworm (Pheretima) is a reddish-brown, segmented worm of phylum Annelida, found in moist soil; it is a 'friend of farmers' because its burrowing and castings improve soil fertility (vermicomposting). Its long body is divided into many segments (metameres); in a mature worm a prominent glandular band, the clitellum, occurs around segments 14–16. The mouth is at the anterior tip below the prostomium. Earthworms are hermaphrodite (each has both male and female organs) but practise cross-fertilisation. Locomotion is by tiny bristles called setae and muscle contraction. The body has a true coelom, a straight digestive tube, a closed circulatory system and a nerve cord.

Cockroach (Periplaneta americana) is an arthropod (insect). Its body is divided into three regions: head (with compound eyes, antennae and mouth parts), thorax (bearing three pairs of legs and two pairs of wings) and abdomen (10 segments). It has a hard chitinous exoskeleton. The digestive system has a crop and a gizzard (for grinding food); blood flows in an open circulatory system (haemolymph in body spaces); excretion is by Malpighian tubules; and breathing is through air tubes called tracheae opening at spiracles. Sexes are separate (sexual dimorphism is seen).

examples.problem: Example 1: What is the clitellum and on which segments is it found in an earthworm?
examples.solution:
The clitellum is a key external feature.

  • It is a prominent glandular band around the body.
  • It is found on segments 14–16 and helps in reproduction (cocoon formation).
examples.answer: The clitellum is a glandular band on segments 14–16 of a mature earthworm, involved in reproduction.

examples.problem: Example 2: Name the three body regions of a cockroach and what the thorax bears.
examples.solution:
An insect body has three regions.

  • Head, thorax and abdomen.
  • The thorax bears three pairs of legs and two pairs of wings.
examples.answer: Head, thorax and abdomen; the thorax bears three pairs of legs and two pairs of wings.

examples.problem: Example 3: How does the cockroach breathe and excrete?
examples.solution:
Insects have characteristic systems.

  • Breathing: through air tubes (tracheae) opening at spiracles.
  • Excretion: by Malpighian tubules.
examples.answer: It breathes through tracheae (opening at spiracles) and excretes via Malpighian tubules.

recap:
• Earthworm (Annelida): segmented (metameres), clitellum on 14–16, hermaphrodite, moves by setae; closed circulation; helps soil fertility.
  • Cockroach (Arthropoda/insect): head + thorax (3 leg pairs, 2 wing pairs) + abdomen; chitin exoskeleton.
  • Cockroach: open circulation (haemolymph), Malpighian tubules for excretion, tracheae for breathing; sexes separate.

quiz.q: The glandular band found on segments 14-16 of an earthworm is the:
quiz.explanation: The clitellum is the reproductive band on segments 14-16.

quiz.q: A cockroach excretes nitrogenous waste using:
quiz.explanation: Insects like the cockroach use Malpighian tubules for excretion.

topics.title: Morphology of the Frog and Its Organ Systems
topics.concept:
The frog (Rana tigrina) is a cold-blooded amphibian that lives both on land and in water. Its body is divided into a head and a trunk (no neck or tail in the adult). The skin is smooth and moist and helps in respiration. Frogs show camouflage (protective colouration) and can change colour slightly. They are able to breathe in three ways: through the skin (cutaneous, especially in water and during hibernation), the buccal cavity, and the lungs (on land). Frogs are poikilothermic and undergo hibernation (winter sleep) and aestivation (summer sleep) to survive extreme conditions.

Its organ systems are well developed:

  • Digestive system — mouth, buccal cavity, oesophagus, stomach, intestine, cloaca; with a liver and pancreas. The frog captures prey with a sticky bilobed tongue.
  • Respiratory system — cutaneous, buccal and pulmonary (lungs) respiration, as above.
  • Circulatory system — a closed system with a three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle); blood has red and white cells and carries materials; lymph also occurs.
  • Reproductive system — sexes are separate; males have a pair of testes, females a pair of ovaries. Fertilisation is external (in water) and development includes a tadpole larva that undergoes metamorphosis into the adult frog.

Frogs are useful to humans: they eat insects and pests (helping agriculture), are part of food chains, and are widely used for biological study.

examples.problem: Example 1: In how many ways can a frog respire, and which is used during hibernation in water?
examples.solution:
Frogs have multiple respiratory routes.

  • Three ways: through the skin (cutaneous), the buccal cavity and the lungs.
  • During hibernation in water, it respires through the skin (cutaneous respiration).
examples.answer: Three ways — cutaneous, buccal and pulmonary; during hibernation in water it uses cutaneous (skin) respiration.

examples.problem: Example 2: How many chambers does the frog's heart have, and what are they?
examples.solution:
The frog has a three-chambered heart.

  • Two atria (auricles) and one ventricle.
examples.answer: Three chambers: two atria and one ventricle.

examples.problem: Example 3: Describe the type of fertilisation and development in frogs.
examples.solution:
Frogs reproduce in water.

  • Fertilisation is external (in water).
  • Development passes through a tadpole larva that undergoes metamorphosis into the adult.
examples.answer: Fertilisation is external (in water); a tadpole larva develops and undergoes metamorphosis into the adult frog.

recap:
• Frog (Rana tigrina): cold-blooded amphibian; body = head + trunk; moist skin aids respiration; shows hibernation & aestivation.
  • Respires in three ways: cutaneous, buccal, pulmonary.
  • Three-chambered heart (two atria, one ventricle); closed circulation.
  • Sexes separate; external fertilisation; tadpole larva → metamorphosis → adult.

quiz.q: The frog's heart has how many chambers?
quiz.explanation: The frog has a three-chambered heart (two atria, one ventricle).
Frogs show external fertilisation in water, followed by a tadpole stage.

questions.q: How many basic types of animal tissue are there?
questions.explanation: Epithelial, connective, muscular and neural — four tissues.

questions.q: Tissue that covers body surfaces and lines organs is:
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue covers surfaces and lines organs and cavities.

questions.q: The most abundant tissue, which links and supports other tissues, is:
questions.explanation: Connective tissue is the most abundant; it links and supports.

questions.q: A ligament connects:
questions.explanation: Ligaments join bone to bone; tendons join muscle to bone.

questions.q: Blood is classified as which type of tissue?
questions.explanation: Blood is a fluid connective tissue that transports materials.

questions.q: Skeletal muscle is:
questions.explanation: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary.

questions.q: Neurons are the main cells of which tissue?
questions.explanation: Neural tissue is made of neurons and glial cells.

questions.q: The earthworm belongs to phylum:
questions.explanation: Earthworms are segmented annelids.

questions.q: The reproductive band on segments 14-16 of an earthworm is the:
questions.explanation: The clitellum is the glandular reproductive band.

questions.q: A cockroach has how many pairs of legs?
questions.explanation: Insects, including cockroaches, have three pairs of legs.

questions.q: The cockroach excretes using:
questions.explanation: Cockroaches use Malpighian tubules for excretion.

questions.q: Cockroaches breathe through air tubes called:
questions.explanation: Insects breathe through tracheae opening at spiracles.

questions.q: The frog is a:
questions.explanation: The frog is a cold-blooded amphibian.

questions.q: The frog's heart has:
questions.explanation: Frogs have a three-chambered heart.

questions.q: Development in frogs passes through which larval stage?
questions.explanation: Frogs develop through a tadpole larva that metamorphoses into the adult.

questions.q: Adipose (fat) tissue is grouped under connective tissue mainly because it:
options: Has cells spaced in a matrix and stores/supports
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue has cells in a matrix and stores fat/insulates — features of connective tissue.

questions.q: An earthworm is called a 'friend of the farmer' because it:
options: Burrows and adds castings, improving soil aeration and fertility
questions.explanation: Its burrowing aerates the soil and its castings enrich it, helping plant growth.

questions.q: The cockroach's open circulatory system means that:
options: Blood (haemolymph) flows freely through body spaces, not always in vessels
Blood is always inside closed vessels
Blood flows only in the heart
questions.explanation: In an open system the haemolymph bathes the organs in body spaces rather than staying in vessels.

questions.q: A frog can survive a dry, hot season buried in mud because it undergoes:
questions.explanation: Aestivation is the summer dormancy that helps the frog survive heat and dryness.

questions.q: The frog's moist skin is important because it:
options: Allows cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through the skin)
questions.explanation: Gas exchange occurs across the moist skin, especially in water and during hibernation.

questions.q: Skeletal, smooth and cardiac muscles differ, but all three share the property of being:
options: Contractile (able to shorten and produce movement)
questions.explanation: All muscle tissue is contractile; they differ in striation and voluntary/involuntary control.
